summary: POC scoping focused on cost modeling and unit economics for Apex's LLM-powered summarization product. Discussed workload sizing, expected token volumes, batching/caching knobs, target latency/budget, and benchmark plan. Agreed on pilot metrics and next steps.
transcript: 00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll keep this tight, agenda is cost modeling, workload sizing, and benchmark planning. 00:18 Sam: Great, thanks Jordan. Quick context — we're building an in-app summarization microservice for enterprise reports, expecting roughly 100k user queries/day average, with peak at 400k. latency target is sub-600ms for 75th pctl, and budget is around $12k/month for inference. 00:45 Priya: Quick clarifying q, when you say queries, what's the token distribution? are those short 50-token prompts or longer? 01:02 Maya: it's mixed, about 60% short (~80 tokens total), 30% medium (~300 tokens), 10% long (~1.2k). That comes from our usage trace — we'll share the CSV. 01:30 Jordan: Okay, so rough weighted avg tokens per request ~300 tokens, so at 100k q/day that's 30M tokens/day. over 30 days ~900M tokens — big number. 01:55 Liam: Our budget assumption of 12k/month — is that pre or post caching/aggregation? 02:10 Jordan: good question. we modeled both — hosted per-token at $0.0008/token for generation + $0.0001/context? um transcription glitch— per 1k tokens maybe— (note: transcription of rates might be off) 02:40 Priya: Let me unpack. For our Dedicated vs Hosted delta: hosted baseline we often estimate $0.0008 per output token and $0.0002 per input token for a large open model; with batching and prefix KV caching we can reduce effective tokens served by ~15-40% depending on duplicate prefixes. 03:10 Sam: 15-40% is a big spread; how do you estimate that? 03:20 Priya: depends on session stickiness and reuse. e.g., if users re-summarize same doc chunks, prefix caching helps. also batching windows — with a 20ms window we can batch small requests for throughput gains but it adds tail latency. 03:45 Maya: latency is important, can't add 100ms extra; 75th pctl under 600ms. 04:00 Jordan: For benchmarking we'll run a 48-hour benchmark with your traces — SE will emulate arrival patterns and measure latencies + tokens, and then we'll produce per-token cost estimates for hosted and dedicated scenarios. 04:22 Priya: We'll include different kernel/quantization profiles — fp16, int8 quant, and a quantized 4-bit profile— note though quality impact needs evals. 04:40 Liam: On networking — we need VPC peering and customer KMS, plus audit logs retained 1 year. 04:55 Jordan: we can support VPC and KMS for Private deployments; for hosted we'll offer encryption at rest and transit, and SOC2 docs. 05:10 Sam: competitor question: we've been talking to Anthropic and Vertex — any differentiators on cost? 05:22 Priya: Our cost controls — batching, caching, quantization recommendations, plus per-route dashboards help. Also can route to cheaper model variants on degrade. 05:40 Maya: Actionable ask — show us per-token math with assumptions so we can compare to their quotes. 05:52 Jordan: we'll send a cost spreadsheet with assumptions (model perf, effective tokens after caching, batching factors, infra amortization) and a draft SOW. 06:05 Priya: On benchmarks — SE needs sample traces, and we should align on success criteria: 75th pctl latency <600ms, cost < $0.0015 per effective token, and quality delta <2% on rouge between quant profiles. 06:25 Sam: Sounds good. Timeline? 06:30 Jordan: Target pilot kickoff in two weeks, benchmark in week one, pilot contract in week three. 06:40 Liam: we'll need internal security review — can you share SOC2 and VPC docs? 06:50 Jordan: yes, sending after call. 07:00 Maya: I'll upload sample traces to the shared sheet. 07:10 Jordan: recap of next steps and owners, thanks all. 07:20 End of recording.
notes: Transcription has small errors (rates slightly garbled). References: benchmark sheet and deck linked in header. Customer provided token distribution CSV promised.
